claim: OraiE180A expression in THD'GAL4 marked dopaminergic neurons leads to complete loss of flight
source: OraiE180A expression in a subset of 21–23 DANs marked by THD' GAL4 (Figure 1B) led to complete loss of flight (Figure 1C)
evidence: Flight bout duration data shown in Figure 1C demonstrates complete loss of flight in THD'>OraiE180A flies compared to controls

claim: THD'GAL4 marks 21-23 dopaminergic neurons including PPL1 and PPM3 clusters
source: OraiE180A expression in a subset of 21–23 DANs marked by THD' GAL4 (Figure 1B)
evidence: Anatomical data shown in Figure 1B with immunolabeling demonstrates the number and location of THD' neurons

claim: Two pairs of PPL1 dopaminergic neurons marked by MB296B contribute significantly to flight deficits
source: Among these 16–19 DANs, two pairs of PPL1 DANs projecting to the γ2α'1 lobes of the MB (marked by the MB296B split GAL4 driver and schematised in Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Aso et al., 2014; Aso and Rubin, 2016) were identified as contributing to the flight deficit to a significant extent (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 1C shows significant flight deficits when OraiE180A is expressed using MB296B driver

claim: Acute inhibition of THD' neurons using Shibirets or TeTxLC leads to severe flight defects
source: Acute activation of either a temperature-sensitive Dynamin mutant (Shibirets; Kitamoto, 2001), which blocks exocytosis at an elevated temperature, or acute expression of the tetanus toxin light chain fragment (TeTxLC; Sweeney et al., 1995), which cleaves Synaptobrevin, an essential component of the synaptic release machinery in THD' neurons, led to severe flight defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 demonstrates severe flight defects upon neuronal inhibition

claim: SOCE is required in THD' neurons during 72-96 hours after puparium formation for flight
source: Abrogation of SOCE by expression of the OraiE180A-dominant-negative transgene at 72–96 hr after puparium formation (APF) resulted in complete loss of flight compared to minor flight deficits observed upon expression of OraiE180A during earlier developmental windows (Figure 1D).
evidence: Temporal expression data in Figure 1D shows that OraiE180A expression specifically during 72-96 hr APF causes complete loss of flight

claim: SOCE is required in THD' neurons during the first 2 days post-eclosion for flight
source: Abrogation of flight also occurred upon OraiE180A expression during the first 2 d post-eclosion (see 'Discussion'), whereas abrogation of SOCE 5 d after eclosion as adults resulted in only modest flight deficits (Figure 1D)
evidence: Temporal expression data in Figure 1D shows flight deficits when OraiE180A is expressed 0-2 days post-eclosion

claim: Loss of SOCE does not alter the number of dopaminergic neurons or affect neurite projection patterns of PPL1 and PPM3 neurons
source: Earlier work has shown that loss of SOCE by expression of OraiE180A does not alter the number of DANs or affect neurite projection patterns of PPL1 and PPM3 neurons (Pathak et al., 2015).
evidence: Previous published work cited demonstrates no changes in neuron number or gross projection patterns

claim: 822 genes are downregulated in THD' neurons upon loss of SOCE
source: Expression of 822 genes was downregulated (with a fold change cut-off of < –1) as assessed using three different methods of differentially expressed genes (DEG) analysis (Figure 1G)
evidence: RNA-seq analysis using three independent DEG methods identified 822 downregulated genes as shown in Figure 1G

claim: 137 genes are upregulated in THD' neurons upon loss of SOCE
source: whereas 137 genes were upregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 6)
evidence: RNA-seq analysis identified 137 upregulated genes as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6

claim: More than 75% of downregulated genes in SOCE-deficient THD' neurons belong to the pupal peak expression cluster
source: A comparison of the proportion of DEGs classified in the larval and pupal clusters revealed that >75% of downregulated genes belonged to the pupal peak (cluster 2), whereas <20% of either the upregulated genes or a random set of genes classified as belonging to the larval peak (Figure 1I).
evidence: Clustering analysis of developmental expression trajectories shown in Figure 1I demonstrates enrichment of downregulated genes in pupal peak cluster

claim: Downregulated genes in SOCE-deficient neurons exhibit higher baseline expression in wildtype pupal THD' neurons
source: Moreover, downregulated genes exhibit higher baseline expression in wildtype pupal THD' neurons (Figure 1—figure supplements 8 and 9).
evidence: Expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 8 and 9 demonstrates higher baseline expression of downregulated genes

claim: Gene Ontology analysis reveals 'Transcription' and 'Ion transporters' as top enriched categories among SOCE-responsive genes
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of SOCE-responsive genes revealed 'Transcription', 'Ion transporters', 'Ca2+ dependent exocytosis', 'GPCRs', 'Synaptic components', and 'Kinases' as top GO categories (Figure 2A). Among these, 'Transcription' and 'Ion transporters' represented categories with the highest enrichment.
evidence: GO analysis results shown in Figure 2A demonstrate enrichment of specific functional categories

claim: Set2 is downregulated in THD' neurons upon loss of SOCE
source: RT-PCRs from sorted THD' neurons confirmed that Set2 levels are indeed downregulated (by 76%) in THD' neurons expressing OraiE180A and to the same extent as seen upon expression of Set2RNAi (79% downregulation; Figure 2C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 2C demonstrates 76% downregulation of Set2

claim: Set2 encodes an H3K36 trimethyltransferase
source: Set1 and Set2 perform methyltransferase activity at H3K4 and H3K36 histone residues, respectively (Ardehali et al., 2011; Stabell et al., 2007).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes Set2 as an H3K36 methyltransferase

claim: Set2 is expressed at fourfold higher levels compared to Set1 in the adult central nervous system
source: In the adult central nervous system (CNS), Set2, is expressed at fourfold higher levels compared to Set1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2; modENCODE Consortium et al., 2010).
evidence: Expression data from modENCODE shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 demonstrates higher Set2 expression

claim: Set2 shows a 5.5-fold increase in expression during the pupal to adult transition
source: Set2 also shows a steep 5.5-fold increase in expression levels during the pupal to adult transition compared to a 2-fold increase in Set1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Developmental expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 demonstrates 5.5-fold increase in Set2 expression

claim: Knockdown of Set2 in THD' neurons results in significant flight defects
source: Knockdown of Set2 in THD' neurons with all four RNAi lines tested resulted in significant flight defects (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 demonstrates flight defects with Set2 knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Set2 rescues flight deficits in OraiE180A-expressing flies
source: Flies expressing OraiE180A in the THD' neurons, which are flightless, exhibit significant rescue in flight bout durations upon Set2 overexpression, through either method (Figure 2D, compare red with purple and brown data)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 2D shows rescue of flight deficits by Set2 overexpression in OraiE180A background

claim: Knockdown of the demethylase Kdm4B rescues flight in THD'>OraiE180A flies
source: That Set2 function downstream of SOCE occurs specifically through its methyltransferase activity was supported through experiments where knockdown of the demethylase Kdm4B, the primary histone demethylase expressed in these neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 6), rescued flight in THD'>OraiEE180A flies (Figure 2D, data in pink).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 2D shows rescue of flight deficits by Kdm4B knockdown in OraiE180A background

claim: Both Set2 depletion and loss of SOCE lead to a decrease in normalized H3K36me3 signal in THD' neurons
source: Moreover, both Set2 depletion and loss of SOCE (THD'>OraiEE180A) lead to a decrease in the normalised H3K36me3 signal in THD' neurons (Figure 2E).
evidence: Immunostaining quantification shown in Figure 2E demonstrates decreased H3K36me3 levels

claim: H3K36me3 is enriched over the gene bodies of SOCE-responsive genes
source: We observed an enrichment of the H3K36me3 signal over the gene bodies of the SOCE-responsive genes (Figure 2F).
evidence: ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2F demonstrates H3K36me3 enrichment on SOCE-responsive genes

claim: Genes with greater downregulation upon loss of SOCE have correspondingly higher H3K36me3 signal
source: Additionally, genes that were more affected by loss of SOCE (greater extent of downregulation) had a correspondingly higher H3K36me3 signal (Figure 2G)
evidence: ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2G demonstrates correlation between H3K36me3 levels and extent of downregulation

claim: E(z) is upregulated upon loss of SOCE
source: Interestingly, another member of the SET domain family, E(z), is upregulated upon loss of SOCE (Figure 2B).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B demonstrates upregulation of E(z)

claim: E(z) is a component of the PRC2 complex which deposits H3K27me3
source: E(z) is a component of the Drosophila PRC2 complex, which represses gene expression through H2K27me3 (Margueron and Reinberg, 2011).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes E(z) as a PRC2 component that deposits H3K27me3

claim: SOCE-responsive genes show higher enrichment of H3K36me3 versus H3K27me3 in wildtype fly heads
source: A comparison of H3K36me3 and H3K27me3 peaks over the 822 SOCE-responsive genes revealed a higher enrichment of H3K36me3 versus H3K27me3 in wildtype fly heads (Figure 2H; modENCODE Consortium et al., 2010)
evidence: ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2H demonstrates higher H3K36me3 enrichment compared to H3K27me3

claim: Feeding GSK343 to SOCE-deficient flies leads to partial rescue of flight in a dose-dependent manner
source: Feeding of GSK343 lead to partial rescue of flight in THD'>OraiEE180A flies in a dose-dependent manner with maximal flight bout durations of up to 400 s (Figure 2J, Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 2J shows dose-dependent rescue of flight by GSK343 treatment

claim: Expression of OraiE180A attenuates the composite ER-Ca2+ release plus SOCE response to carbachol in PPL1 DANs
source: In support of this idea, either expression of OraiE180A or knockdown of the IP3R attenuated the composite ER-Ca2+ release plus SOCE response to carbachol (CCh), a mAChR agonist, in PPL1 DANs (Figure 3B–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3B-D demonstrates attenuated CCh response with OraiE180A expression

claim: Knockdown of Set2 abrogates the Ca2+ response to carbachol in PPL1 DANs
source: Importantly, knockdown of Set2 also abrogated the Ca2+ response to CCh (Figure 3B–D)
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3B-D demonstrates loss of CCh response with Set2 knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Set2 rescues the Ca2+ response in OraiE180A-expressing neurons
source: whereas overexpression of a transgene encoding Set2 in THD' neurons either with loss of SOCE (OraiE180A) or with knockdown of the IP3R (itprRNAi) leads to significant rescue of the Ca2+ response, indicating that Set2 is required downstream of SOCE (Figure 3B–D)
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3B-D demonstrates rescue of CCh response by Set2 overexpression

claim: Loss of SOCE leads to downregulation of itpr (72%) and mAChR (56%) in THD' DANs
source: Loss of SOCE upon expression of OraiE180A leads to a significant decrease in the expression of itpr (72% downregulation; Figure 3E) and mAChR (56% downregulation; Figure 3E) in THD' DANs.
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 3E demonstrates downregulation of itpr and mAChR

claim: Knockdown of Set2 leads to downregulation of itpr (43%), mAChR (78%), and Stim (61%) in THD' neurons
source: Importantly, knockdown of Set2 in THD' neurons also led to downregulation of itpr (43%), mAChR (78%), and Stim (61%) (Figure 3E).
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 3E demonstrates downregulation of multiple genes with Set2 knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Set2 in the OraiE180A background rescues expression levels of itpr (69% increase), mAChR (43% increase), and Stim (40% increase)
source: Overexpression of Set2 in the background of OraiE180A led to a rescue in the levels of itpr (69% increase), mAChR (43% increase), and Stim (40% increase) (Figure 3E).
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 3E demonstrates rescue of gene expression by Set2 overexpression

claim: Trl/GAF has the highest enrichment value and lowest p-value among identified transcription factors with binding sites enriched in SOCE-regulated genes
source: Among the top 10 identified TFs, the homeobox TF Trl/GAF had the highest enrichment value, lowest p-value (Figure 4B), and was consistently expressed in the CNS through all developmental stages, with a distinct peak during pupal development (Figure 4B, lower panel).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B identifies Trl as top candidate with highest enrichment and lowest p-value

claim: Knockdown of Trl in THD' neurons results in significant flight deficits
source: To test the functional significance of Trl/GAF, we tested flight in flies with THD'-specific knockdown of Trl using two independent RNAi lines (Figure 4C) as well as in existing Trl mutant combinations that were viable as adults (Figure 4—figure supplement 2). While homozygous trl null alleles are lethal, trans-heterozygotes of two different hypomorphic alleles were viable and exhibit significant flight deficits (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 4C shows significant flight deficits with Trl knockdown

claim: Flight deficits caused by Trl knockdown can be rescued by Set2 overexpression
source: Moreover, the flight deficits caused by TrlRNAi specifically in the THD' neurons could be rescued by Set2 overexpression (Figure 4C, compare data in red and brown).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 4C shows rescue of Trl knockdown flight deficits by Set2 overexpression

claim: Heteroallelic combination of trl13C with STIMKO causes significant flight deficits which can be rescued by overexpression of STIM or Set2
source: While STIMKO/+ flies demonstrate normal flight bout durations, adding a single copy of the trl13C allele to the STIMKO heterozygotes (STIMKO/+; trl13C/+ trans-heterozygotes) resulted in significant flight deficits, which could be rescued by overexpression of either STIM or Set2 (Figure 4D).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 4D demonstrates genetic interaction between Trl and STIM and rescue by Set2 overexpression

claim: A single copy of trl13C in combination with single copies of various itpr mutant alleles shows significant reduction in flight bout duration
source: A single copy of trl13C placed in combination with a single copy of various itpr mutant alleles also showed a significant reduction in the duration of flight bouts (Figure 4—figure supplement 3)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 demonstrates genetic interaction between Trl and IP3R

claim: Knockdown of Trl results in downregulation of Set2 (32%), itpr (56%), and mAchR (73%) in THD' neurons
source: Set2 has 20 Trl binding sites in a 2 kb region upstream of the transcription start site (Figure 4—figure supplement 4) and knockdown of Trl resulted in downregulation of Set2 (32%) and the Set2-regulated genes itpr (56%) and mAchR (73%; Figure 4E).
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 4E demonstrates downregulation of multiple genes with Trl knockdown

claim: Trans-heterozygotic combination of hypomorphic Trl alleles has markedly reduced levels of brain H3K36me3
source: Moreover, a trans-heterozygotic combination of hypomorphic Trl alleles (trl13C/62) had markedly reduced levels of brain H3K36me3 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 4F demonstrates reduced H3K36me3 levels in Trl mutants

claim: Trl knockdown in fpDANs exhibits strongly attenuated responses to cholinergic stimulation
source: Compared to WT fpDANs, which respond robustly to cholinergic stimulation, TrlRNAi-expressing DANs exhibit strongly attenuated responses (Figure 4G–I).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4G-I demonstrates attenuated CCh response with Trl knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Set2 rescues the cholinergic response in Trl knockdown neurons
source: Overexpression of Set2 in the TrlRNAi background rescued the cholinergic response (Figure 4G–I).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4G-I demonstrates rescue of CCh response by Set2 overexpression in Trl knockdown background

claim: Overexpression of Trl is unable to rescue the loss of flight caused by loss of SOCE
source: Overexpression of Trl, however, is unable to rescue the loss of flight caused by loss of SOCE (THD'>OraiEE180A; Figure 5A).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 5A shows no rescue of OraiE180A flight deficits by Trl overexpression

claim: Trl transcript levels are unchanged in the OraiE180A condition
source: Moreover, Trl transcript levels are unchanged in the OraiE180A condition (Figure 5B).
evidence: qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B demonstrates no change in Trl transcript levels with OraiE180A expression

claim: Multiple classes of ion channel genes including Na+, K+, and Cl- channels are downregulated in fpDANs upon expression of OraiE180A
source: 'Ion transport' is among the top GO terms identified in SOCE-responsive genes (Figure 2A). Indeed, multiple classes of ion channel genes, including several Na+, K+, and Cl- channels, are downregulated in fpDANs upon expression of OraiE180A (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5D and E demonstrates downregulation of multiple ion channel genes

claim: NaCP60E, para, cac, ca-α1D, hk, and eag are downregulated between 0.6- and 0.9-fold upon Trl knockdown
source: NaCP60E, para (Na+ channels), cac, ca-α1D (VGCC subunits), hk, and eag (outward-rectifying K+ channels) are all downregulated between 0.6- and 0.9-fold upon Trl knockdown (Figure 5G)
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 5G demonstrates downregulation of ion channel genes with Trl knockdown

claim: PPL1 DANs exhibit a robust Ca2+ response to KCl-evoked depolarization that is lost upon knockdown of Trl
source: To test the functional consequences of altered ion channel gene expression downstream of Trl, neuronal activity of the fpDANs was tested by means of KCl-evoked depolarisation. PPL1 DANs exhibited a robust Ca2+ response that was lost upon knockdown of Trl (Figure 5H–J, data in orange).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5H-J demonstrates loss of KCl response with Trl knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Trl in THD+ DANs does not rescue the KCl response in PPL1 DANs with loss of SOCE
source: In consonance with the earlier behavioural experiments (Figure 5A), overexpression of Trl+ in THD+ DANs did not rescue the KCl response in PPL1 DANs with loss of SOCE (OraiE180A; TrlOE, Figure 5I and J)
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5I and J demonstrates no rescue of KCl response by Trl overexpression in OraiE180A background

claim: Response to KCl is lost in PPL1 neurons by knockdown of Set2
source: Response to KCl is also lost in PPL1 neurons by knockdown of Set2 and restored to a significant extent by overexpression of Set2 in THD' DANs lacking SOCE (OraiE180A;Set2OE; Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6A-C demonstrates loss of KCl response with Set2 knockdown

claim: Overexpression of Set2 in THD' DANs lacking SOCE restores the KCl response to a significant extent
source: Response to KCl is also lost in PPL1 neurons by knockdown of Set2 and restored to a significant extent by overexpression of Set2 in THD' DANs lacking SOCE (OraiE180A;Set2OE; Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6A-C demonstrates rescue of KCl response by Set2 overexpression in OraiE180A background

claim: Treatment with nimodipine abrogates the depolarization response to KCl in PPL1 neurons
source: We confirmed that the KCl response of PPL1 neurons requires VGCC function either by treatment with nimodopine (Xu and Lipscombe, 2001), an L-type VGCC inhibitor, or by knockdown of a conserved VGCC subunit cac (cacRNAi). Both forms of perturbation abrogated the depolarisation response to KCl in PPL1 neurons (Figure 6D–F, data in purple or orange, respectively).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6D-F demonstrates loss of KCl response with nimodipine treatment

claim: Knockdown of cac abrogates the depolarization response to KCl in PPL1 neurons
source: We confirmed that the KCl response of PPL1 neurons requires VGCC function either by treatment with nimodopine (Xu and Lipscombe, 2001), an L-type VGCC inhibitor, or by knockdown of a conserved VGCC subunit cac (cacRNAi). Both forms of perturbation abrogated the depolarisation response to KCl in PPL1 neurons (Figure 6D–F, data in purple or orange, respectively).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6D-F demonstrates loss of KCl response with cac knockdown

claim: Ca2+ entry upon KCl-mediated depolarization in PPL1 neurons is a cell-autonomous property
source: Moreover, the Ca2+ entry upon KCl-mediated depolarisation in PPL1 neurons is a cell-autonomous property as evident by measuring the response after treatment with the Na+ channel inhibitor, tetrodotoxin (TTX; Figure 6D–F, data in magenta).
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6D-F demonstrates maintained KCl response with TTX treatment, indicating cell-autonomous property

claim: All four VGCC subunits (cac, ca-α1D, ca-α1T, and ca-β) are downregulated upon loss of SOCE in THD' DANs
source: All four subunits of Drosophila VGCC are downregulated upon loss of SOCE (OraiE180A; Figure 6H) in THD' DANs
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 6H demonstrates downregulation of VGCC subunits

claim: Overexpression of Set2 in the OraiE180A background restores expression of the four VGCC subunits tested
source: whereas overexpression of Set2 in the background of OraiE180A restored expression of the four VGCC subunits tested (Figure 6H)
evidence: qRT-PCR data from FAC-sorted neurons shown in Figure 6H demonstrates rescue of VGCC subunit expression by Set2 overexpression

claim: Knockdown of each of the four VGCC subunits independently in PPL1 neurons results in significant loss of flight
source: The functional significance of downregulation of VGCC subunits by the SOCE-Trl-Set2 pathway was tested directly by knockdown of the four VGCC subunits independently in PPL1 neurons followed by measurement of flight bout durations. Significant loss of flight was observed with knockdown of each subunit (Figure 6I)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 6I demonstrates flight deficits with knockdown of individual VGCC subunits

claim: Loss of flight upon loss of SOCE cannot be restored by overexpression of cac alone
source: This idea is further supported by the observation that loss of flight upon loss of SOCE cannot be restored by overexpression of cac alone (Figure 6J)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 6J shows no rescue of OraiE180A flight deficits by cac overexpression alone

claim: Inhibition of THD' DANs from 72 to 96 hr APF using Kir2.1 results in significant flight deficits
source: Inhibition of THD' DANs from 72 to 96 hr APF using acute induction of the inward-rectifying K+ channel Kir2.1 (Johns et al., 1999) or optogenetic inhibition through the hyperpolarising Cl- channel GtACR2 (Govorunova et al., 2015) resulted in significant flight deficits (Figure 7A, data in dark or light green).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7A demonstrates flight deficits with Kir2.1-mediated inhibition during 72-96 hr APF

claim: Optogenetic inhibition of THD' DANs through GtACR2 from 72 to 96 hr APF results in significant flight deficits
source: Inhibition of THD' DANs from 72 to 96 hr APF using acute induction of the inward-rectifying K+ channel Kir2.1 (Johns et al., 1999) or optogenetic inhibition through the hyperpolarising Cl- channel GtACR2 (Govorunova et al., 2015) resulted in significant flight deficits (Figure 7A, data in dark or light green).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7A demonstrates flight deficits with GtACR2-mediated inhibition during 72-96 hr APF

claim: Hyperactivation of THD' neurons through CsChrimson or TrpA1 stimulation from 72 to 96 hr APF results in flight deficits
source: Similar flight defects were recapitulated upon hyperactivation of THD' neurons through either optogenetic (CsChrimson; Klapoetke et al., 2014) or thermogenetic (TrpA1; Viswanath et al., 2003) stimulation (Figure 7A, data in orange or red)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7A demonstrates flight deficits with CsChrimson or TrpA1-mediated hyperactivation during 72-96 hr APF

claim: NachBac expression rescues both flight and excitability in fpDANs lacking SOCE
source: To test whether restoring excitability in fpDANs lacking SOCE (THD'>OraiEE180A) is sufficient to restore flight, we induced hyperexcitability by overexpressing NachBac (Nitabach et al., 2006), a bacterial Na+ channel. NachBac expression rescued both flight (THD'>OraiEE180A; Figure 7B) and excitability (Figure 7C–E).
evidence: Flight assay and calcium imaging data shown in Figure 7B-E demonstrate rescue by NachBac expression

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of THD'>OraiE180A DANs using CsChrimson at 72-79 hr APF or 0-2 d post eclosion results in partial rescue of flight
source: A partial rescue of flight was also obtained by optogenetic stimulation of neuronal activity through activation of THD'>OraiEE180A DANs using CsChrimson either 72–79 hr APF or 0–2 d post eclosion (Figure 7E).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7E demonstrates partial rescue by optogenetic stimulation during critical periods

claim: Excess K+ supplementation partially rescues flight in animals lacking SOCE in THD' DANs
source: Moreover, inducing neuronal hyperactivation with indirect methods such as excess K+ supplementation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) or impeding glial K+ uptake, by genetic depletion of the glial K+ channel sandman (Weiss et al., 2019; Figure 7—figure supplement 2), partially rescued flight in animals lacking SOCE in the THD' DANs.
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 demonstrates partial rescue by K+ supplementation

claim: Genetic depletion of the glial K+ channel sandman partially rescues flight in animals lacking SOCE in THD' DANs
source: Moreover, inducing neuronal hyperactivation with indirect methods such as excess K+ supplementation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) or impeding glial K+ uptake, by genetic depletion of the glial K+ channel sandman (Weiss et al., 2019; Figure 7—figure supplement 2), partially rescued flight in animals lacking SOCE in the THD' DANs.
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 7—figure supplement 2 demonstrates partial rescue by sandman knockdown

claim: THD'>OraiE180A flies fed on GSK343 show a rescue in KCl responses, with enhanced response in fliers compared to non-fliers
source: THD'>OraiEE180A flies fed on GSK343 showed a rescue in KCl responses, with a clearly enhanced response in the fliers compared to the non-fliers (Figure 7—figure supplement 3C)
evidence: Calcium imaging data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3C demonstrates rescue of KCl response by GSK343 treatment, with correlation to flight ability

claim: Loss of SOCE results in striking changes in neurite volume within the γ2α'1 lobe MB
source: Striking changes in the neurite volume upon expression of OraiE180A were observed. Importantly, these changes could be rescued to a significant extent by restoring either Set2 (OraiE180A; Set2OE) or by inducing hyperactivity through NachBac expression (OraiE180A; NachBacOE; Figure 8C and D).
evidence: Super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 8C and D demonstrates changes in neurite volume with OraiE180A expression

claim: Restoring Set2 rescues neurite volume changes in the γ2α'1 lobe MB caused by loss of SOCE
source: Striking changes in the neurite volume upon expression of OraiE180A were observed. Importantly, these changes could be rescued to a significant extent by restoring either Set2 (OraiE180A; Set2OE) or by inducing hyperactivity through NachBac expression (OraiE180A; NachBacOE; Figure 8C and D).
evidence: Super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 8C and D demonstrates rescue of neurite volume by Set2 overexpression

claim: Inducing hyperactivity through NachBac expression rescues neurite volume changes in the γ2α'1 lobe MB caused by loss of SOCE
source: Striking changes in the neurite volume upon expression of OraiE180A were observed. Importantly, these changes could be rescued to a significant extent by restoring either Set2 (OraiE180A; Set2OE) or by inducing hyperactivity through NachBac expression (OraiE180A; NachBacOE; Figure 8C and D).
evidence: Super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 8C and D demonstrates rescue of neurite volume by NachBac expression

claim: Loss of SOCE attenuates dopamine release at the γ2α'1 region of the MB
source: Loss of SOCE (THD'>OraiEE180A) attenuated DA release (Figure 8E–G), which could be partially rescued by overexpression of Set2.
evidence: GRAB-DA sensor measurements shown in Figure 8E-G demonstrate attenuated dopamine release with OraiE180A expression

claim: Overexpression of Set2 partially rescues dopamine release in SOCE-deficient neurons
source: Loss of SOCE (THD'>OraiEE180A) attenuated DA release (Figure 8E–G), which could be partially rescued by overexpression of Set2.
evidence: GRAB-DA sensor measurements shown in Figure 8E-G demonstrate partial rescue of dopamine release by Set2 overexpression

claim: THD' neurons receive cholinergic inputs that stimulate store Ca2+ release through the IP3R, leading to SOCE through Orai
source: It is known that THD'-marked PPL1 DANs receive cholinergic inputs that stimulate store Ca2+ release through the IP3R, leading to SOCE through Orai (Figure 3A; Ebihara et al., 2006; Sharma and Hasan, 2020).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes cholinergic inputs stimulate IP3R-mediated Ca2+ release and SOCE

claim: H3K36me3 is a marker for transcriptional activation enriched in gene bodies of actively transcribed genes
source: Both these markers are epigenetic signatures for transcriptional activation, where H3K4me3 is enriched at the 5′ end of the gene body and H3K36me3 is enriched in the gene bodies of actively transcribed genes; schematised in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
evidence: Established knowledge about histone modifications and their roles in transcription

claim: H3K27me3 is a repressive signature which silences transcription
source: While H3K36me3 is a marker for transcriptional activation (Krogan et al., 2003), H3K27me3 is a repressive signature which silences transcription (Cai et al., 2021).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes H3K27me3 as a repressive histone mark

claim: Deposition of H3K36me3 allosterically inhibits the PRC2 complex, preventing it from depositing H3K27me3 at the same genomic loci
source: These two marks are antagonistic as deduced from studies which have shown that deposition of H3K36me3 allosterically inhibits the Polycomb Repressive Complex (PRC2), thereby preventing it from depositing the H3K27me3 signature at the same genomic loci (Finogenova et al., 2020).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates antagonistic relationship between H3K36me3 and H3K27me3

claim: Set2 is the only Drosophila methyltransferase specific for H3K36 trimethylation
source: Set2 encodes the only Drosophila methyltransferase which is specific for H3K36 trimethylation (Stabell et al., 2007).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes Set2 as the sole H3K36 trimethyltransferase in Drosophila

claim: Drosophila genome encodes a single member of the NFAT gene family which is insensitive to intracellular Ca2+ and SOCE
source: Unlike mammals, the Drosophila genome encodes a single member of the NFAT gene family, which does not possess calcineurin binding sites, and is therefore insensitive to intracellular Ca2+ and SOCE (Keyser et al., 2007).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes that Drosophila NFAT is Ca2+-insensitive

claim: Trl interacts with diverse proteins primarily through its BTB-POZ domain
source: Although Trl does not possess a defined Ca2+ binding domain, it interacts with a diverse set of proteins, primarily through its BTB-POZ domain (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) as demonstrated earlier by affinity purification of Trl from embryonic extracts followed by high-throughput mass spectrometry (Lomaev et al., 2017).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl protein interactions through BTB-POZ domain

claim: Trl is phosphorylated at threonine residue T237
source: Among the identified interacting partners, we focused on kinases, keeping in mind an earlier study in Drosophila indicating phosphorylation of Trl at a threonine residue (T237; Zhai et al., 2008).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl phosphorylation at T237

claim: CamKII is implicated in flight in THD' neurons
source: Analysis of the Trl interactome revealed several kinases, which were expressed to varying extents in the THD' neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), including the Ca2+-dependent CamKII, implicated earlier in flight in THD' neurons (Ravi et al., 2018).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes CamKII role in flight in THD' neurons

claim: Loss of CamKII in THD' neurons by RNAi-mediated knockdown or peptide inhibitor expression results in significant flight deficits
source: Loss of CamKII in THD' neurons by RNAi-mediated knockdown or through expression of a peptide inhibitor (Ala; Mehren and Griffith, 2004) resulted in significant flight deficits (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 demonstrates flight deficits with CamKII loss

claim: Acute expression of constitutively active CamKIIT287D in OraiE180A background from 72 to 96 hr APF results in weak rescue of flight
source: Acute expression of CamKIIT287D in the OraiE180A background using the TARGET system (McGuire et al., 2004) resulted in a weak rescue of flight when implemented from 72 to 96 hr APF (Figure 5—figure supplement 4)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 5—figure supplement 4 demonstrates weak rescue by constitutively active CamKII

claim: Overexpression of WT CamKII or phosphorylation-incompetent CamKIIT287A fails to rescue flight in OraiE180A background
source: whereas overexpression of WT CamKII or a phosphorylation-incompetent allele (CamKIIT287A) failed to rescue flight (Figure 5—figure supplement 4)
evidence: Flight assay data in Figure 5—figure supplement 4 demonstrates no rescue by WT or phosphorylation-incompetent CamKII

claim: Trl utilizes a Q-rich intrinsically disordered domain to self-multimerize or interact with accessory proteins
source: In vitro studies on Drosophila Trl reveal that it utilises a Q-rich intrinsically disordered domain (IDD) to self-multimerise or interact with a wide range of accessory proteins (Wilkins and Lis, 1999).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl multimerization through IDD

claim: Multimeric complexes of Trl reside on chromatin with exceptionally long residence time and maintain chromatin in an 'open' state
source: Multimeric complexes of Trl reside on chromatin with an exceptionally long residence time and maintain chromatin in an 'open' state (Tang et al., 2022).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl's role in maintaining open chromatin

claim: Trl directly interacts with components of the transcription initiation and elongation complex
source: Trl has also been reported to directly interact with components of the transcription initiation and elongation complex (Chopra et al., 2008; Li et al., 2013)
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl interactions with transcription machinery

claim: Trl supports long-distance promoter-enhancer interactions
source: support long-distance promoter–enhancer interactions (Mahmoudi et al., 2003)
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl role in promoter-enhancer interactions

claim: Trl mediates active ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling by maintaining nucleosome-free stretches
source: mediate active ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling by maintaining nucleosome-free stretches (Tsukiyama et al., 1994)
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl role in chromatin remodeling

claim: Trl regulates global gene expression by controlling transcriptional stalling and pausing
source: and regulate global gene expression by controlling transcriptional stalling and pausing (Tsai et al., 2016)
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl role in transcriptional regulation

claim: Trl plays a role in chromatin folding in Drosophila neurons to enable cell type-specific gene expression
source: A recent study demonstrates a role for Trl in chromatin folding in Drosophila neurons to enable cell type-specific gene expression (Mohana et al., 2023).
evidence: Published literature cited demonstrates Trl role in chromatin folding and cell type-specific gene expression

claim: Neurons undergo maturation of electrical properties with gradual increase in depolarizing responses and synaptic transmission over pupal development
source: Neurons undergo maturation of their electrical properties with a gradual increase in depolarising responses and synaptic transmission over the course of pupal development (Järvilehto and Finell, 1983).
evidence: Published literature cited establishes developmental maturation of neuronal electrical properties

claim: Set2 has 20 Trl binding sites in a 2 kb region upstream of the transcription start site
source: Set2 has 20 Trl binding sites in a 2 kb region upstream of the transcription start site (Figure 4—figure supplement 4)
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4 identifies Trl binding sites in Set2 regulatory region

claim: Ca2+ influx through SOCE sustains Trl activation through CamKII
source: These data support a model (schematised in Figure 5C) wherein Ca2+ influx through SOCE sustains Trl activation, in part through CamKII, leading to expression of Set2 followed by increased levels of chromatin H3K36me3 marks that drive further downstream gene expression changes through a transcriptional feedback loop.
evidence: Genetic rescue experiments with constitutively active CamKII and model schematic in Figure 5C support this mechanism

claim: SOCE-driven Set2-mediated H3K36me3 enhances expression of key GPCRs, components of intracellular Ca2+ signaling, and ion channels for optimal dopaminergic neuron function
source: SOCE-driven Set2-mediated H3K36me3 enhances the expression of key GPCRS, components of intracellular Ca2+ signalling (Figure 2A) and ion channels (Figure 6A and B) for optimal dopaminergic neuron function (Figure 7D–F) and flight (Figure 1C).
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence from GO analysis, gene expression data, and functional assays support this conclusion
